desc:
A partition of the string s cuts it into one or more consecutive non-empty pieces whose concatenation is s. Count the partitions in which every piece is a palindrome. Two partitions are different when they cut s at different places.

Return the count modulo 1,000,000,007.

For example, "aab" has 2 such partitions (a|a|b and aa|b), "aaa" has 4 (a|a|a, aa|a, a|aa, aaa) and "abc" has 1.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Listing every partition is far too slow, since the number of partitions can be exponential. Count them instead.
Let ways[i] be the number of palindromic partitions of the prefix of length i. The last piece of such a partition is some palindromic suffix of that prefix.
ways[i] = sum of ways[j] over all j < i for which s[j..i-1] is a palindrome, with ways[0] = 1. Find all palindromic substrings by expanding around each of the 2n-1 centers.
editorial: Define ways[i] as the number of palindromic partitions of s[0..i-1], with ways[0] = 1 for the empty prefix. Look at the last piece of a partition of the prefix of length i: it is a palindrome s[j..i-1] and what remains before it is any palindromic partition of the prefix of length j. Hence ways[i] is the sum of ways[j] over all j such that s[j..i-1] is a palindrome. Different last pieces give different partitions, so nothing is double counted.

To know which substrings are palindromes, expand around every center and record, for each end index, the list of start indices of palindromes that end there. There are at most O(n2) palindromic substrings (for example in aaa...a), so this table takes O(n2) time and space in the worst case.
The answer is ways[n] modulo 1,000,000,007. For aaa...a every cut is allowed, so the answer is 2n-1, which is a useful check.
solution:
def countPalindromePartitions(s):
    MOD = 10**9 + 7
    n = len(s)
    starts = [[] for _ in range(n)]  # starts[e]: start indices of palindromes ending at e
    for c in range(n):
        l = r = c
        while l >= 0 and r < n and s[l] == s[r]:
            starts[r].append(l)
            l -= 1
            r += 1
        l, r = c, c + 1
        while l >= 0 and r < n and s[l] == s[r]:
            starts[r].append(l)
            l -= 1
            r += 1
    ways = [0] * (n + 1)
    ways[0] = 1
    for e in range(n):
        total = 0
        for st in starts[e]:
            total += ways[st]
        ways[e + 1] = total % MOD
    return ways[n]
